text:
We have become obsessed with the "calendar density" metric, equating a back-to-back schedule with high productivity. But a full calendar is often just a proxy for shallow work. 

Think about the person who spends eight hours jumping between fifteen different 30-minute syncs. On paper, they are incredibly busy. In reality, they have zero capacity for deep, creative thought. We need to stop measuring success by how many slots we fill and start measuring it by how much meaningful progress we actually make.
